answer: The network mandates 6,000 megabytes of memory-hard work to gate each agent, functioning like a prism that refracts tasks into distinct memory-resident compute sessions. Each agent must populate a unique crystal structure of state data within its allocated heap; the verifier detects overlaps as invalid state leaks. An honest agent pays for one unit of cost, while 1,000 fakes incur 1,000 times that cost, as each inhabits a separate garden of RAM.
